title: Match day
summary: Planning a night at the stadium: what you will do, how you get there, and how it went. Along the way you get polite verbs and the particles that hold a sentence together.
canDo: I can say what I do and what I will do.
I can say when, where and how I am going somewhere, and arrange to meet.
I can say what I did and who I did it with.

items.back: Polite verb ending for habits and the future. Japanese has no separate future tense.
items.note: サッカーを{見|み}ます。 I watch / will watch football.
ビールを{飲|の}みません。 I don't drink beer.

items.back: Marks the thing the action is done to. Said "o". The verb always comes last.
items.note: チケットを{買|か}います。 I'll buy a ticket.

items.back: What will you do? / What do you do?
"Won't you…?" A polite invitation, softer than a plain question.
items.note: {一緒|いっしょ}に{見|み}ませんか。 Shall we watch it together?

items.back: Sounds good! / That's nice. The standard way to accept or approve.
に after a clock time or date = "at / on".
items.note: {七時|しちじ}に{始|はじ}まります。 It starts at seven.

items.front: スタジアム{へ|e}{行|い}きます
items.back: へ (said "e") marks the direction you move in. With 行きます you can also use に.
items.note: スタジアムに{行|い}きます means the same.

items.back: で marks the place where an action happens.
items.note: スタジアムでチケットを{買|か}います。

items.back: で also marks the means: by train, by bus, with chopsticks.
items.note: {何|なに}で{行|い}きますか。 How are you getting there?

items.front: {何時|なんじ}に{始|はじ}まりますか

items.note: サッカーを{見|み}ました。 I watched football.
ビールを{飲|の}みませんでした。 I didn't drink beer.
{中村|なかむら}さんと{見|み}ました。 I watched it with Nakamura-san.

items.front: どのチームが{勝|か}ちましたか
items.back: が marks who did it when that is the new information. A question word as the subject takes が, and so does the answer.
items.note: {東京|とうきょう}が{勝|か}ちました。 Tokyo won.

lessons.title: What are you doing tomorrow?
lessons.canDo: I can say what I will do, say what I won't, and invite someone along.

meme.top: English: I watch, I will watch, I am going to watch
meme.bottom: Japanese: ます. One form. Done.

intro.scene: Back in the hostel lounge. There is a match on tomorrow night.

lines.text: レオさん、{明日|あした}{何|なに}をしますか。
lines.meaning: Leo, what are you doing tomorrow?

lines.text: サッカーを{見|み}ます。{中村|なかむら}さん{は|wa}？
わたし{は|wa}{何|なに}もしません。
じゃあ、{一緒|いっしょ}に{見|み}ませんか。
lines.meaning: Then shall we watch it together?

lines.text: いいですね！ビールも{飲|の}みます。
lines.meaning: Sounds good! I'll have a beer too.

notes.title: 〜ます: now, usually, and tomorrow
notes.body: The polite verb ending. It covers habits and the future, so {見|み}ます is both "I watch" and "I will watch". Words like {明日|あした} tell you which. The negative is 〜ません.

notes.title: を and the verb at the end
notes.body: を (said "o") marks the thing you act on, and the verb always closes the sentence: サッカーを{見|み}ます, literally "football [o] watch".

notes.title: 〜ませんか = an invitation
notes.body: Turning the negative into a question makes a gentle invitation: {見|み}ませんか, "won't you watch?". Accept with いいですね. {何|なに}も + negative means "nothing".

exercises.prompt: Which one means "I don't drink beer"?
options: ビールを{飲|の}みません。
ビールじゃありません。
exercises.explain: Verbs use 〜ません. じゃありません is for nouns: "it isn't beer".

exercises.answer: チケットを{買|か}います

exercises.prompt: Listen. What are you being asked?
exercises.text: {明日|あした}{何|なに}をしますか。

exercises.context: {一緒|いっしょ}に{見|み}ませんか。

exercises.prompt: Ask in Japanese: "What are you doing tomorrow?"
exercises.answer: {明日|あした}{何|なに}をしますか。
alt: {明日|あした}{は|wa}{何|なに}をしますか。
{明日|あす}{何|なに}をしますか。

lessons.title: Getting to the stadium
lessons.canDo: I can say how and when I'm going somewhere and arrange where to meet.

meme.bottom: Three tiny syllables. One large headache. You've got this.

intro.scene: The next morning, sorting out the plan.

lines.text: スタジアム{へ|e}{何|なに}で{行|い}きますか。
lines.meaning: How are we getting to the stadium?

lines.text: {電車|でんしゃ}で{行|い}きます。{六時|ろくじ}に{新宿駅|しんじゅくえき}で{会|あ}いませんか。
lines.meaning: By train. Shall we meet at Shinjuku station at six?

lines.text: いいですよ。{試合|しあい}{は|wa}{何時|なんじ}に{始|はじ}まりますか。
lines.meaning: Sure. What time does the match start?

lines.text: {七時|しちじ}に{始|はじ}まります。スタジアムでチケットを{買|か}います。
lines.meaning: It starts at seven. I'll buy the tickets at the stadium.

notes.title: に: a point in time, a destination
notes.body: {六時|ろくじ}に = at six. スタジアムに{行|い}きます = I go to the stadium. Think of に as a pin on a clock or a map.

notes.title: へ: the direction
notes.body: Written へ, said "e". With verbs of movement it means "towards", and for going somewhere it is interchangeable with に: スタジアム{へ|e}{行|い}きます.

notes.title: で: where it happens, and how
notes.body: The place of an action: {駅|えき}で{会|あ}います, スタジアムで{買|か}います. And the means: {電車|でんしゃ}で{行|い}きます. So {何|なに}で{行|い}きますか asks "by what?".

exercises.text: {七時|しちじ}___{始|はじ}まります。

exercises.explain: Meeting is an action that happens there, so it is で.

exercises.answer: スタジアム{へ|e}{行|い}きます
alt: スタジアムに{行|い}きます

exercises.text: {何時|なんじ}に{始|はじ}まりますか。

exercises.prompt: Which one means "I'll buy a ticket at the stadium"?
options: スタジアムでチケットを{買|か}います。
スタジアムにチケットを{買|か}います。
スタジアムをチケットで{買|か}います。
exercises.explain: Place of the action: で. Thing bought: を.

exercises.prompt: Type in Japanese: "I'm going by train."
exercises.answer: {電車|でんしゃ}で{行|い}きます。
alt: わたし{は|wa}{電車|でんしゃ}で{行|い}きます。
{私|わたし}{は|wa}{電車|でんしゃ}で{行|い}きます。

lessons.title: So, how was the game?
lessons.canDo: I can say what I did, what I didn't do, and who I was with.

meme.top: Me: I'll just have one beer

intro.scene: The day after. Sato wants the full report.

lines.text: レオさん、{昨日|きのう}{何|なに}をしましたか。
lines.meaning: Leo, what did you do yesterday?

lines.text: {中村|なかむら}さんとサッカーを{見|み}ました。
いいですね。どのチームが{勝|か}ちましたか。
{東京|とうきょう}が{勝|か}ちました！でも、わたし{は|wa}ビールを{飲|の}みませんでした。
lines.meaning: Tokyo won! But I didn't drink any beer.

lines.text: {中村|なかむら}さんが{全部|ぜんぶ}{飲|の}みました。

notes.title: The four polite forms
notes.body: {見|み}ます watch · {見|み}ません don't watch · {見|み}ました watched · {見|み}ませんでした didn't watch. Every verb follows this pattern; only the part before ます changes from verb to verb.

notes.title: と = with
notes.body: After a person, と means "together with": {中村|なかむら}さんと{見|み}ました. (After a noun in a list it means "and".)

notes.title: が: who did it
notes.body: When the doer is the news, mark it with が. A question word as subject always takes が, and the answer keeps it: どのチームが{勝|か}ちましたか → {東京|とうきょう}が{勝|か}ちました.

exercises.text: {昨日|きのう}サッカーを{見|み}___。

exercises.prompt: Which one means "I didn't drink beer"?
options: ビールを{飲|の}みませんでした。
ビールを{飲|の}みません。
ビールを{飲|の}みました。
exercises.explain: 〜ません = don't / won't. 〜ませんでした = didn't.

exercises.answer: {東京|とうきょう}が{勝|か}ちました
